title: Bolshevik seizure of power
note: The October Revolution brought the Bolsheviks to power; seizure of government did not immediately secure control of Russia.

title: Assembly dissolved; civil war deepens
note: The Constituent Assembly was dispersed and Brest-Litovsk ended Russia’s war with Germany; civil war encouraged coercive government.

title: Kronstadt, NEP and the faction ban
note: Economic retreat towards limited markets accompanied tighter political discipline.

title: Stalin becomes General Secretary
note: Party appointments became an important institutional resource in the succession struggle.

title: Lenin dies
note: Stalin used shifting alliances and ideological positioning during a multi-year struggle for supremacy.

title: First Five-Year Plan begins
note: Industrial priorities and coercive agricultural change reshaped Soviet society.

title: Forced collectivisation accelerates
note: The drive to restructure agriculture brought resistance, repression and severe disruption.

title: Show trials and new constitution
note: Formal rights coexisted with escalating terror; test the gap between legal claims and political practice.

title: Great Terror peaks, 1937–1938
note: Repression extended beyond prominent party leaders through mass operations.

title: Tehran Conference
note: Wartime cooperation coexisted with concerns about the future European settlement.

title: Yalta and Potsdam
note: German defeat removed the common enemy; disagreements over Poland, reparations and security deepened.

title: Truman Doctrine and Marshall Plan
note: Aid and containment linked economic recovery to competing interpretations of security.

title: Berlin Blockade, 1948–1949
note: The airlift frustrated Soviet pressure and accelerated the division of Germany.

title: NATO, Soviet atomic test and PRC
note: Alliance formation and a changing nuclear and Asian balance widened the rivalry.

title: Korean War, 1950–1953
note: Containment became a major military conflict with decisive Korean and Chinese agency.

title: Batista’s coup
note: The closure of constitutional politics helped radicalise opposition.

title: Moncada attack
note: A military failure subsequently became a symbol of revolutionary legitimacy.

title: Stalin dies
note: New leadership opened possibilities for negotiation without ending bloc rivalry.

title: Hungarian uprising suppressed
note: De-Stalinisation did not mean accepting the loss of Soviet control in Eastern Europe.

title: Granma landing
note: Survivors established the Sierra Maestra guerrilla campaign alongside urban opposition.

title: Cuban Revolution
note: Batista fled on 1 January; revolutionary victory preceded the consolidation of a communist state.

title: Nationalisation and CDRs
note: Economic transformation and neighbourhood organisation intertwined mobilisation and surveillance.

title: Bay of Pigs and Berlin Wall
note: US-backed invasion failed in Cuba; the Wall stemmed migration while entrenching Germany’s division.

title: Literacy campaign
note: Mass mobilisation expanded education while tying reform to revolutionary identity.

title: Cuban Missile Crisis
note: Nuclear confrontation ended through public and private compromises, largely without Cuban control of negotiations.

title: Hotline and Partial Test Ban Treaty
note: Crisis management improved, but rivalry and the arms race continued.

title: Cuban Communist Party
note: A consolidated party framework institutionalised revolutionary rule.

title: Prague Spring suppressed
note: The limits of sovereignty within the Soviet bloc were reaffirmed.

title: Sino-Soviet border clashes
note: Ideological rivalry and national-security competition split the communist world.

title: Ten-million-ton sugar target missed
note: The campaign exposed the costs of mobilisation and continued sugar dependence.

title: China visit and SALT I
note: Triangular diplomacy and arms agreements managed competition without eliminating it.

title: Helsinki and Angola
note: European diplomacy advanced while conflict in Africa exposed the geographic limits of détente.

title: Cuban socialist constitution
note: Formal institutions developed within a one-party political structure.

title: Soviet intervention in Afghanistan
note: The intervention intensified confrontation, but détente had already been weakening.

title: Solidarity and renewed confrontation
note: Dissent in Poland and renewed superpower pressure exposed the limits of bloc control.

title: SDI and heightened nuclear tension
note: Arms competition and mutual fears raised the costs and dangers of confrontation.

title: Gorbachev takes power
note: Reform and new thinking gradually transformed Soviet domestic and foreign policy.

title: INF Treaty
note: An entire category of land-based intermediate-range missiles was eliminated.

title: Eastern European revolutions
note: Non-intervention enabled changes that weakened the bloc; the Berlin Wall opened on 9 November.

title: Soviet Union dissolves
note: USSR collapse followed the ending of bipolar confrontation; these are connected but distinct outcomes.

title: Cuba’s Special Period deepens
note: Loss of Soviet support forced adjustment but did not produce regime collapse.
